scope: All visitor-visible story text: headline, The Story, The LAiDIES Read, What This Means for You, cocktail line and class notes. Every factual paraphrase is source-derived and counted at each visible occurrence.
countingMethod: Count every source-derived fragment where it appears. Only the linked learning recommendation is editorial authority.

fragments.text: OpenAI says it temporarily paused new sign-ups and upgrades to ChatGPT Pro $200, also called Pro 20X, on September 10.
Pro 20X is OpenAI’s name for its ChatGPT Pro $200 tier.
The pause applies if you are on Free, Go, Plus or Pro $100 and want to move into Pro $200.
This is a pause on joining or upgrading into that tier.
It is not an automatic cancellation: OpenAI says existing Pro $200 subscriptions continue to renew as usual.
Pro $100 remains available for a new upgrade.
If you already pay for Pro $200, the Help Center says it keeps renewing as usual.
But if you cancel, finish a downgrade, or a renewal failure ends the plan, OpenAI says you cannot buy Pro $200 again until the pause lifts.
If you were planning to upgrade, the Help Center says new moves into Pro $200 are paused.
That is the whole consumer consequence: an active plan and a new purchase follow different rules right now.
Before you change or cancel Pro $200, read OpenAI’s pause FAQ. It says a scheduled cancellation or downgrade keeps Pro $200 active until the billing cycle ends; a change that takes effect ends it.
“A Pro $200 sign-up pause blocks a new purchase or upgrade.
It does not by itself cancel an active Pro $200 subscription.”
A pause on new purchases and a change to an active subscription are different events.
Working with AI 101: Trusting the Output and Checking It helps you check which event an official rule actually describes before changing something you already use.
fragments.rationale: Internal learning guidance; it makes no additional external product assertion.

sources.limitOrigin: Official Help Center record, conservative source ceiling.
